A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ParalESN research. Their main texts, figures, tables, equations and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching material across the reordered appendices.

before.justification: V1 reports original memory, forecasting and classification experiments, computational measurements, and appendix sensitivity analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains those original results and adds S4 training results, real-valued ablations, deep-model sensitivity analyses and ParalESN results on Long Range Arena. The literature-derived LRA comparator scores are distinguished from the work's own results.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the complex diagonal recurrence, initialization, dense first-layer and ring inter-layer input matrices, convolutional mixer and trained readout. The ring structure highlighted in v2's Figure 1 already appears in v1's Equation 5. The real-valued variant is introduced as an ablation control, without revising the proposed ParalESN procedure.

E1.justification: V2 adds actual evaluation on four Long Range Arena tasks: Image, ListOps, Text and PathFinder (Appendices E.4 and G.5). These extend coverage to text, structured expressions and visual path reasoning. The original memory, forecasting, UEA/UCR and MNIST tasks remain.

E2.justification: S4 becomes an evaluated comparator on sMNIST and psMNIST in Table 4. The new LRA comparison additionally includes Reformer, BigBird, Linear Transformer, Performer, S5 and RWKV, using literature-derived comparator scores. The existing SCR and Structured RC comparison is retained, moving from v1 Table 9 to v2 Table 13.

E3.justification: Existing splits, the 24-hour Bayesian search budget and the 100-epoch training cap remain. V2 adds a two-layer S4 configuration with hidden size 172, evaluated on a different GPU, and an LRA comparison using published baseline scores. Appendix F.1 revises the reported V100 count from four to one; this does not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V2 adds deep-model hyperparameter sensitivity, including depth, concatenation and inter-layer settings (Figure 7), real-versus-complex ablations across memory and forecasting tasks (Tables 11–12), and a parameter-count analysis (Table 10). It also revises the shallow phase-sensitivity curve in Figure 6. The original structured-reservoir comparison remains.

E5.justification: The existing plus/minus reporting, sensitivity distributions and Figure 3 Wilcoxon comparison remain. Neither version specifies repeated-run counts or seeds. Added result rows do not introduce a new uncertainty-estimation or testing procedure; the new LRA table provides point estimates.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 and existing Table 4 entries retain their numerical results. New S4 entries lead the MNIST comparisons at 99.2% and 97.9%; new ablation, parameter-count and deep-sensitivity results substantially expand the evidence. Table 14 adds ParalESN's LRA results, averaging 63.7%. Figure 6 also changes the shallow theta_max sensitivity findings.

T1.justification: Proposition 4.2 changes from unrestricted exact equivalence to an almost-sure statement under i.i.d. entries with a density. V2 adds a substantive universality proof in Appendix D.3, including a filter-perturbation lemma and stochastic Lp extension, replacing v1's unsupported passage from approximate diagonalizability to exact equivalence. The ESP necessity argument also now addresses the unit-modulus boundary.

C1.justification: V2's abstract consolidates the benchmark-specific accuracy claims into a general competitive-accuracy statement and drops the explicit claim of orders-of-magnitude energy savings. The central claims about parallel processing, scalable reservoirs, ESP, universality and computational efficiency remain.

C2.justification: V2 adds an oscillatory-dynamics explanation for complex eigenvalues and argues that faster hyperparameter search partly mitigates sensitivity. It acknowledges weaker LRA performance than several trained sequence models and qualifies S4 efficiency measurements because of different hardware. These additions refine the interpretation and applicability boundaries without replacing the main conclusions.

D1.justification: V2 adds a ParalESN code-availability link, an S4 implementation reference and architecture details, and an LRA dataset-size table. It explicitly identifies the provenance of LRA comparator results and revises the hardware disclosure. Most existing preprocessing, optimizer, readout and hyperparameter-search details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: New citations support diagonalizability and matrix bounds, complex-valued representations, LSTM attribution, LRA and RWKV. The principal positioning relative to RC, LRU and state-space models remains. Updates to existing S4, S5 and Verzelli references represent bibliographic changes rather than newly introduced prior work.

P1.justification: Prose is extensively revised across the abstract, method exposition, experimental discussion and appendices. Section 3 moves the scaling discussion before the equations; definitions now precede proofs through the C/D appendix swap; comparator descriptions are consolidated in Appendix F.2. These are substantial editorial changes beyond the added scientific content.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn to expose diagonal/ring structure and mixer operations. V2 adds the extensive deep-sensitivity Figure 7 and five tables covering LRA datasets, parameter counts, ablations and LRA results. Table 4 and Figure 5 gain S4, while Figure 6 and several table headers are reformatted. Existing tables are also relocated and renumbered.

improvement.justification: The real-valued ablation, deep sensitivity study and LRA evaluation substantially strengthen and qualify the empirical case beyond v1's benchmarks. Revised equivalence assumptions and the perturbation analysis also address an important gap in v1's theory. Residual proof problems, notably Appendix D.3's incorrect geometric-series factor, and S4's different timing hardware limit these gains, but the stronger support for the central design and clearer applicability boundaries provide a substantial net improvement.
